title: Refute Printed.globalPrincipalValueConverse_normTwist_ideal_subset_bergman (Thm 6.3.2.2(1), p. 310)
body:
Closes #4861

Refutes `Printed.globalPrincipalValueConverse_normTwist_ideal_subset_bergman` (Theorem 6.3.2.2(1), range after (6.3.2.20), p. 310) in `RiemannMasullo/Ch06_LocalGlobal/Sec3_Printed.lean`.

**Counterexample.** F = ℚ, χ = 1, t = 0, S = ∅, and the entire multiplier u(s) = exp(-s²)/Γ(s/2) (instead of the docstring's exp(s⁴): it cancels the gamma factor, so no Stirling estimate is needed). For Re s > 1, ζ̂_ℚ(s) = Γℝ(s) ζ(s) (from `continuedCompletedHeckeL_spec`, `completedHeckeL_one_eq_dedekindZeta` and Dedekind zeta of ℚ = Riemann zeta), so the product is s(s-1) π^(-s/2) ζ(s) exp(-s²). On the strip 3 ≤ Re s ≤ 4 its modulus is at least 2 π^(-2) (2 - π²/6) exp((Im s)² - 16), using |ζ(s) - 1| ≤ π²/6 - 1 for Re s ≥ 2. A Schwartz–Bergman element is bounded on that strip, and agreeing off a discrete set gives points of agreement near 7/2 + iT for every T, a contradiction.

**Helpers** (private, directly above the theorem): `..._false_zeta` (lower bound for ζ on Re s ≥ 2), `..._false_completed` (ζ̂_ℚ = Γℝ·ζ on Re s > 1), `..._false_lower` (the modulus bound). Added Mathlib imports: `Mathlib.Analysis.Real.Pi.Bounds`, `Mathlib.NumberTheory.LSeries.Dirichlet`, `Mathlib.NumberTheory.LSeries.RiemannZeta`, `Mathlib.NumberTheory.ZetaValues`; and `open Topology in` before the theorem.
